sanskrit: divo jāto divas putro yasmāj jātaṃ mahat sahaḥ | aśvattham agre jaitrāya- -acchā devaṃ vadāmasi ||
english: Born of heaven, son of heaven, from whom great might was born — to the aśvattha tree first, for victory, we speak, addressing the divine one.

sanskrit: taṃ tvāśvā yathā ratham upa tiṣṭhantu rājānaḥ | samitibhyo vivaktave ||
english: As horses stand ready beside a chariot, so may kings attend upon you — to speak forth at assemblies.

sanskrit: tvayā vayaṃ devajāta sarvāḥ prāśo jayāmasi | uta satyā utānṛtāḥ ||
english: With you, O god-born one, may we win all the contests — both those that are just and those that are not.

sanskrit: yo aśvatthena mitreṇa samitīr avagacchati | jayāt sa sarvāḥ pṛtanā yāś ca satyā utānṛtāḥ ||
english: He who goes to assemblies with the aśvattha as his ally — may he conquer all battles, both those that are just and those that are not.

sanskrit: adharāñco nir dravantu samityā ululākṛtāḥ | aśvatthamitraṃ puruṣaṃ ye vācā pṛtanyān ||
english: May they flee downward, driven out from the assembly with ululation — those who with words attack the man whose ally is the aśvattha.

sanskrit: ugrā nāma stha teṣāṃ vaḥ puro gṛhāḥ prācī dik teṣāṃ vo agnir iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata dvipade catuṣpade teṣāṃ vo yāny āyudhāni yā iṣavas tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: You are named the Fierce Ones; their houses are in front of you; the eastern quarter is yours; fire is their arrow. May they be gracious to us, to the two-footed and four-footed. To their weapons, to their arrows — homage to them, svāhā!

sanskrit: kravyā nāma stha teṣāṃ vo dakṣiṇā gṛhā dakṣiṇā dik teṣāṃ va āpa iṣavaḥ | (…) ||
english: You are named the Flesh-Eaters; their houses are to the south of you; the southern quarter is yours; water is their arrow. [May they be gracious to us, to the two-footed and four-footed. To their weapons, to their arrows — homage to them, svāhā!]

sanskrit: virājo nāma stha teṣāṃ vaḥ paścād gṛhāḥ pratīcī dik teṣāṃ vaḥ kāma iṣavaḥ | (…) ||
english: You are named the Resplendent Ones; their houses are behind you; the western quarter is yours; desire is their arrow. [May they be gracious to us, to the two-footed and four-footed. To their weapons, to their arrows — homage to them, svāhā!]

sanskrit: avasthā nāma stha teṣāṃ va uttarād gṛhā udīcī dik teṣāṃ vo vāta iṣavaḥ | (…) ||
english: You are named the Abiding Ones; their houses are to the north of you; the northern quarter is yours; wind is their arrow. [May they be gracious to us, to the two-footed and four-footed. To their weapons, to their arrows — homage to them, svāhā!]

sanskrit: uttare nāma stha teṣāṃ va upari gṛhā ūrdhvā dik teṣāṃ vo varṣam iṣavaḥ | te no mṛḍata dvipade catuṣpade teṣāṃ vo yāny āyudhāni yā iṣavas tebhyo namas tebhyaḥ svāhā ||
english: You are named the Superior Ones; their houses are above you; the upward quarter is yours; rain is their arrow. May they be gracious to us, to the two-footed and four-footed. To their weapons, to their arrows — homage to them, svāhā!

sanskrit: yadīdaṃ devo diva ājagāma yady antarikṣād yadi pārthivo yaḥ | yadi yajño yajñapateḥ svargas tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo namasā vidhema ||
english: Whether this deity has come from heaven, or from the atmosphere, or the one that is earthly — whether it be the sacrifice, whether the heaven of the lord of the sacrifice — to all of them together may we offer homage.

sanskrit: yam indram āhur varuṇaṃ yam āhur yaṃ mitram āhur yam u somam āhuḥ | yam agnim āhur yam u sūryam āhus tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo namasā vidhema ||
english: Him whom they call Indra, whom they call Varuṇa, whom they call Mitra, and whom they call Soma — him whom they call Agni, and whom they call Sūrya — to all of them together may we offer homage.

sanskrit: ye śmaśānāni manasā nayanti sūryasya raśmīn anusaṃcaranti | ye devānām ṛtvijo yajñiyānāṃ tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo namasā vidhema ||
english: Those who with their minds lead souls to the cremation grounds, who move along the rays of the sun — those who are the officiating priests of the sacrifice-worthy gods — to all of them together may we offer homage.

sanskrit: ye tandriyā jalpyā prorṇuvanti svapnaṃ durbhūtam abhi ye kiranti | ye devānāṃ dharmadhṛto babhūvus tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo namasā vidhema ||
english: Those who spread forth languor and incoherent babbling, who scatter ill-being and evil dreams — those who have become the upholders of the divine order — to all of them together may we offer homage.

sanskrit: svabhyasair abhi ye bhāyante ye bhāḥ kṛṇvanti ya u rodayanti | ye vā strīṇāṃ pratirūpā babhūvus tebhyaḥ sarvebhyo namasā vidhema ||
english: Those who terrify with their own brilliances, who create radiances, and who cause weeping — or those who have taken on the likeness of women — to all of them together may we offer homage.
